title: Arithmetic and Geometric Sequences
seo_title: Algebra I Arithmetic and Geometric Sequences Worksheets (TEKS A.12D)
standard_text: A.12C identify terms of arithmetic and geometric sequences when the sequences are given in function form using recursive processes; A.12D write a formula for the nth term of arithmetic and geometric sequences, given the value of several of their terms
meta_desc: Free Algebra I sequence worksheets for Texas TEKS A.12C and A.12D: arithmetic and geometric sequences, nth term formulas, recursive formulas and problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Arithmetic adds d; geometric multiplies by r.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Arithmetic: add the same number d each time. an = a1 + (n − 1)d.
  • Geometric: multiply by the same number r. an = a1 · rn−1.
  • A recursive formula uses the term before: an = an−1 + 4.

Examples

Example

5, 9, 13, 17, …: find a20

d = 4

5 + 19 × 4

Answer: 81

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Using n instead of n − 1The first term has no added d.
Adding the ratioGeometric means multiply.
Mixing up a1 and da1 is the first term.

Write a formula for the nth term of arithmetic and geometric sequences, given the value of several of their terms.
No. It is geometric with r = 2.

faq.q: Is an arithmetic sequence a linear function?

items.q: Is this sequence arithmetic, geometric or neither? 16, 25, 36, 49, 64, …
items.e: The differences change (9, 11, 13, 15) and there is no common ratio, so it is neither.

items.q: What is the next term? 3, 9, 27, 81, …
items.e: This is geometric: multiply by 3 each time. 81 × 3 = 243.

items.q: What is the next term? 16, 28, 40, 52, …
items.e: This is arithmetic: add 12 each time. 52 + 12 = 64.

items.q: Is this sequence arithmetic, geometric or neither? 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, …
items.e: Each term is the one before × 2, so it is geometric.

items.q: The sequence 5, 15, 45, … is geometric. What is the 5th term?
items.e: Keep multiplying by 3: 5, 15, 45, 135, 405. The 5th term is 405.

items.q: Which recursive formula gives the sequence 5, 20, 80, 320, …?
items.e: Each term is the one before times 4: a1 = 5; an = 4 · an−1.

items.q: A sequence is defined by a1 = 4 and an = (−2) · an−1. What is a5?
items.e: Start at 4 and multiply by −2 each time: 4, −8, 16, −32, 64. So a5 = 64.

items.q: A sequence is defined by a1 = 5 and an = 3 · an−1. What is a5?
items.e: Start at 5 and multiply by 3 each time: 5, 15, 45, 135, 405. So a5 = 405.

items.q: Which explicit formula gives the sequence 4, 10, 16, 22, …?
items.e: For an arithmetic sequence, an = a1 + d(n − 1). Here a1 = 4 and d = 6: an = 4 + 6(n − 1).

items.q: A sequence is defined by a1 = −2 and an = an−1 − 3. What is a5?
items.e: Start at −2 and subtract 3 each time: −2, −5, −8, −11, −14. So a5 = −14.

items.q: Which explicit formula gives the sequence 10, 20, 40, 80, …?
items.e: For a geometric sequence, an = a1 · rn − 1. Here a1 = 10 and r = 2: an = 10 · 2n − 1.

items.q: Which recursive formula gives the sequence 3, −6, 12, −24, …?
items.e: Each term is the one before times −2: a1 = 3; an = (−2) · an−1.

items.q: Which explicit formula gives the sequence 5, 20, 80, 320, …?

items.q: Which recursive formula gives the sequence 7, 11, 15, 19, …?
items.e: A recursive formula gives the first term and how to get each term from the one before: a1 = 7; an = an−1 + 4.

items.q: A ball is dropped from 200 cm. Each bounce reaches half the height of the one before. How high is the 3rd bounce?
Patterns are made from sticks: 4, 7, 10, 13, … sticks. How many sticks are in pattern 20?
items.e: The nth term is 3n + 1. Pattern 20: 3 × 20 + 1 = 61.

items.q: A bacteria population doubles every hour. It starts at 50. How many are there after 5 hours?
items.e: 50 → 100 → 200 → 400 → 800 → 1,600. This is a geometric sequence with ratio 2.

items.q: A car worth $16,000 loses half its value every 3 years. What is it worth after 9 years?
What is the next triangular number? 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, …
items.e: The differences go up by 1: +2, +3, +4, +5, so add 6: 21.

items.q: The nth term of a sequence is 50 − 4n. What is the first negative term?
A theater has 20 seats in row 1, 23 in row 2, 26 in row 3, and so on. How many seats are in row 15?
How many terms of 7, 11, 15, 19, … are less than 100?
items.e: The nth term is 4n + 3. 4n + 3 < 100 when n < 24.25, so 24 terms.

items.q: A geometric sequence has a1 = 5 and r = 2. Which is a8?
Ethan says 2, 6, 18, 54, … is arithmetic because the numbers go up. Is he right?
c: No, it is geometric with ratio 3
items.e: The differences are 4, 12, 36, which are not equal. Each term is × 3: geometric with ratio 3.
